parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Planets have been observed orbiting a star in another solar system. Measurements are made of the orbital radius $r$ and the time period $T$ of each of these planets.

The variation with $R^3$ of $T^2$ is shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

The relationship between $T$ and $R$ is given by

$$T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2R^3}{GM}$$

where $G$ is the gravitational constant and $M$ is the mass of the star.

Determine the mass $M$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: A rock of mass $m$ is also in orbit around the star in (b). The radius of the orbit is $r$.
parts.text: Explain why the gravitational potential energy of the rock is negative.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the kinetic energy $E_{\text{k}}$ of the rock is given by

$$E_{\text{k}} = \frac{GMm}{2r}.$$

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use the expression in (c)(ii) to derive an expression for the total energy of the rock.
